taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station T-14 (survey area T). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 161.1 | 3.39 | 3.39
2 | 1022.2 | 1.76 | 5.15
3 | 85.2 | 1.93 | 7.08
4 | 88.8 | 9.77 | 16.85
5 | 117.4 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as Q-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Station: T-14
Curve type: Not Q-type as logged — the resistivity sequence (161.1 → 1022.2 → 85.2 → 88.8 → 117.4 Ω·m) rises sharply then falls then rises again, which is a K/H-type pattern, not the monotonically decreasing sequence that defines a true Q-type curve. This discrepancy should be flagged for re-interpretation before final reporting.
Aquifer depth: approximately 5.15–16.85 m (Layers 3–4, 85.2–88.8 Ω·m), representing the low-resistivity zone beneath the resistive Layer 2 cap.
Recommendation: Plan drilling to at least ~17 m to fully penetrate the probable water-bearing interval between 5.15 and 16.85 m; expect a resistive, likely dry/compact zone (1022 Ω·m) above 5.15 m that may require casing. Request QC review of the VES curve classification, as the raw resistivity sequence does not support the Q-type designation on file.
